title: U-Harmony: Enhancing Joint Training for Segmentation Models with Universal Harmonization
mechanism: Per-instance feature harmonization, then restoration layers that reinject dataset-specific statistics into the decoder. A domain-gated head infers each domain's contribution from prototypes, so no dataset ID is needed at test.
adaptation: A source-gated decoder for the case where the source is unknown or shifted (E1 half-cut CSIR, benchmark new-module track). Check whether the gate picks CSIR on E1.
min_experiment: Arm = house PF + harmonize/restore + gated head (3 seeds) versus house PF. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2 and test crack IoU. Kill if E1 relF1@2 < +0.02 and test is n.d.
evidence: R: cross-institution brain lesion datasets; a secondary summary reports up to +8.4% DSC (unverified against the full paper).
prior_overlap: per-panel BN adaptation failed, but that was test-time BN statistics, not learned dataset-gated restoration

alt_notes.adaptation: Source-gated decoder for cells of unknown source (benchmark new-module track, WattCycle's future rig); compare gate-chosen source with the true source on E1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: U-Harmony gated decoder, 5 seeds, no source ID at test vs source-FiLM arm with true ID and house PF; metric clean-49 crack IoU and E1 relF1@2; kill if it does not reach at least half of the source-FiLM gain.
